title: Wedding Day at Troldhaugen: Grieg and Vetter
work: Wedding Day at Troldhaugen, Op. 65 No. 6
question: How do Grieg and Harald Vetter differ in treating this wedding march as a dance?
intro: More guests than expected arrived at Troldhaugen for Edvard and Nina Grieg’s silver wedding on 11 June 1892. Four years later Grieg wrote a piano piece on the occasion, Wedding Day at Troldhaugen. His own 1903 recording shortens the piece to two minutes; Harald Vetter plays it complete.

recordings.label: Edvard Grieg
recordings.note: The composer played his own abridged version in Paris in 1903, with the march fitted onto a short disc.

recordings.label: Harald Vetter
recordings.note: The complete piece, recorded on 4 October 2006, includes the quiet middle section and the return of the march.

passages.label: Opening march over low octaves
passages.note: The march rests on low octaves and short, clipped chords. Triplets in the right hand lead into the next phrase.

passages.label: March with firmer bass
passages.note: The march continues with firmer bass notes beneath the right hand’s chords.

passages.label: March in full chords
passages.note: The piano plays the march in full chords and keeps the short, quick figures between the heavier beats.

alignment.scope: Shared opening material only; the complete source recordings remain unedited. No whole-work tempo ratio.
alignment.note: An exploratory 4–94 / 5–120 second map had low-confidence opening points and a plateau near reference 90–91.5 seconds. Inspection against the measured 46/62-second and 74/98-second changes supported the shared passage but not the shortened ending. The published map excludes both uncertain ends; its remaining path was inspected and has no point below 0.8. No pitch transposition or audio edit was applied.
